lines.text: Forms and a grid are already available. Build the pickup: still, rise and fall, add turning, add swelling; then walk wedges to five completed cubes on a platform.
Four cumulative demonstrations remain available. Five completed pickups make the same operations an encounter in a small level.
Three gaps: a floor carries you, a cube grows to meet the banks, a plank turns into a passage. What relation makes each crossing possible?
Moving the cube is not yet carrying the rider.
The visible surface and the collision have to grow together.
The centre stays; the ends travel.
Into depth, sideways, upwards. The same carrier makes a different journey when one coordinate changes.
Cubes rise and fall along the route. Transport makes contact possible; collection leaves a difference behind.
The middle stays. One end rises while the other descends; a centred blade can become a climb to another grid level.
Walk through x, y, z and their combination. Ten degrees with each row: the far end can look flat while the route to it has become difficult.
A repeated angle makes a corridor. You need time to walk what the program has already assembled.
Five profiles, one layered speed rule. What does the shape make you notice about the same motion?
The proportions survive. The door becomes possible.
Drink me: the room grows, the body stays, the table becomes a descent.

lines.note: The catalyst does not damage the creature, it changes its state, and the whole argument of the chamber is that folded is not less: a transformation done to a body is contact, not harm.

note_src.quote: the catalyst's effect on the creature is a state transition rather than damage

lines.text: the pit: push and grow. a transform done to you.

lines.note: Here the transform is done to you, and the arithmetic that was neutral while it acted on objects is not neutral once the space it acts on is inhabited.
